w1104-01-zombie-ant.text: A zombie ant fungus is steering this ant away from its colony. Three weeks ago, a spore landed on it and grew inside its body. Now it climbs a plant, about twenty five centimeters up, where the air suits the fungus. [curious] So what does it do up there? At noon, it bites the vein under a leaf... and its jaw locks. It dies hanging there. Days later, a stalk grows out of the back of its head and rains spores onto the forest floor. [warmly] The fungus wins, the ant loses, and in AP Bio that's PARASITISM.

w1104-02-sodium-lake.text: In 1947, crews mixed sodium and water... using a whole lake. America had tons of leftover sodium from the war, in old, leaking drums, and no one would ship it. So crews rolled the drums off a cliff onto frozen Lake Lenore and shot holes in them. And the lake exploded. [curious] Why? Sodium has just ONE electron in its outer shell, and it gives it up easily. Water grabs that electron, making hydrogen gas and heat... and the heat lights the hydrogen. That's why sodium is stored under oil. Free practice for this on levlprep dot com.

w1104-03-stunt-airbag.text: This stuntman is about to drop onto a stunt airbag, eight stories down. He'll hit it at close to fifty miles an hour. [curious] So how does a bag of air save him? Either way, his body has to lose all that speed. Concrete would do it in a split second, and that takes a HUGE force. [thoughtful] But the airbag sinks and lets out air... so his stop lasts many times longer, and the average force on him gets many times smaller. In AP Physics, that's impulse: he loses the same momentum either way, just spread over more time. Then he rolls off, and the crew resets the bag.
